chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 20th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 8 regions counts equally, so one carries 12% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 3rd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.214, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26, but from the 2nd highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 2nd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 21st lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 19 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 7th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.232, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 10th steepest fall of 26, but from the 5th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 10th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 5th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 18 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 15th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.23, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.

rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.236, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 10th steepest fall of 26, but from the 4th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 10th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 4th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 22nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 21 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The joint 9th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2001, 2021 and 2023
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.189, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 5th steepest fall of 26, but from the 4th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 5th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 4th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 22nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 19 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 20th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.165, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 6th steepest fall of 26, but from the 5th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 6th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 5th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 22nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 41 regions counts equally, so one carries 2% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 5th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.209, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 9th steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 9th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 5th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 22nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 13 regions counts equally, so one carries 8% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 20th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.194, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 2nd steepest fall of 26, but from the 3rd highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 2nd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 3rd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 23rd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 79 regions counts equally, so one carries 1% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 22nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.211, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 12th steepest fall of 26, but from the 2nd highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 12th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 2nd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 31 regions counts equally, so one carries 3% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The joint 13th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2001
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.194, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 2nd steepest fall of 26, but from the 2nd highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 2nd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 2nd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 23rd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 47 regions counts equally, so one carries 2% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The joint 22nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2010
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.114, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 2nd steepest fall of 26, but from the 3rd highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 2nd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 3rd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 24th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 17 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 23rd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.168, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 13th steepest fall of 26, but from the 3rd highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 13th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 3rd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 24th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 39 regions counts equally, so one carries 3% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 13th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.226, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 15th steepest fall of 26, but from the 6th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 15th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 6th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 24th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 12 regions counts equally, so one carries 8% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 14th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.214, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 25th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 5 regions counts equally, so one carries 20% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The joint 21st most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2004
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 7 regions counts equally, so one carries 14% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 26th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.139, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 8th steepest fall of 26, but from the 1st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 8th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 31 regions counts equally, so one carries 3% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 24th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.182, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26, but from the 1st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 7 regions counts equally, so one carries 14% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 25th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.212, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 22nd steepest fall of 26, but from the 1st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 22nd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.176, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.statement: The 7th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 2nd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions, NOT area-weighted
aggregate.caveat: each of the 8 regions counts equally, so one carries 12% of this figure whatever its cropland area. Where one region holds most of the crop the country figure understates it. No sensitivity score is emitted because it cannot be computed without crop area per region.

severity.statement: The 24th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: roughly one country in seven sits at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.183, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 3rd steepest fall of 26, but from the 1st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 3rd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.

Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.
